Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 69, verse 5–8:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast (al-Taghiyah)﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿As for Thamud﴾, the people of Salih, Allah destroyed them by the Taghiyah.

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of al-Taghiyah by which Allah destroyed Thamud. Some of them said: it is their transgression (tughyan) and their disbelief in Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿they were destroyed by the Taghiyah﴾, he said: "By their sins."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Taghiyah﴾, then he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿Thamud denied by their transgression (bi-taghwaha)﴾, and said: "This Taghiyah is their transgression and their disbelief in the signs of Allah. The Taghiyah is their transgression by which they transgressed in the disobedience of Allah and in opposition to the Book of Allah."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they were destroyed by the cry (al-sayhah) which exceeded the measures of crying and surpassed them.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Taghiyah﴾: Allah sent upon them a cry which annihilated them.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿by the Taghiyah﴾, he said: Allah sent upon them a single cry which annihilated them.

The most correct of the two views regarding this is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: they were destroyed by the overwhelming cry.

We only said that this is more correct because Allah informed about Thamud with the means by which He destroyed them, just as He informed about 'Ad with that by which He destroyed them, saying: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾. If the report about Thamud concerned the cause by which He destroyed them, the report about 'Ad would also be like that, since it is in one context; and His following that with His report about 'Ad, that their destruction was by the wind, is clear evidence that His report about Thamud is what I have explained.

* *

His saying: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: As for 'Ad, the people of Hud, Allah destroyed them by a furious wind (rih sarsar), which is extremely violent in its blowing, along with its intense coldness, ﴿'atiyah﴾, meaning: it rebelled against its keepers (kharazah) in its blowing, so it exceeded in its violence and blowing its known measure in blowing and coldness.

Those of the scholars of interpretation said similar to what we said regarding that.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious wind﴾, he said: "By a destructive, cold wind, which rebelled against them without mercy or blessing, constant and never ceasing."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious wind﴾; and al-Sarsar: the cold one, which rebelled against them until it pierced their hearts.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Allah has never sent any wind except by measure, nor sent down any drop except by weight, except on the day of Noah and the day of 'Ad. For the water on the day of Noah overflowed its keepers, so they had no power over it. Then he recited: ﴿When the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾. And the wind rebelled against its keepers, so they had no power over it. Then he recited: ﴿with a furious, violent wind﴾."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Abu Sinan narrated to us, from more than one, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, who said: "No drop of water ever descended except by measure at the hands of an angel; but when it was the day of Noah, He permitted the water without the keepers, so the water overflowed the mountains and came out, and that is the saying of Allah: ﴿When the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾. And no wind ever descended except by measure at the hands of an angel, except on the day of 'Ad, for He permitted it without the keepers, so it came out, and that is the saying of Allah: ﴿with a furious, violent wind﴾: it rebelled against the keepers."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿with a furious, violent wind﴾: "Al-sarsar: the violent one, and al-'atiyah: the overpowering one which rebelled against them and overpowered them."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿sarsar﴾, he said: "Violent."

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿with a furious wind (sarsar)﴾, meaning: cold and rebellious, which rebelled against them without mercy or blessing.

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they were destroyed by the cry (al-sayhah) which exceeded the measures of crying and surpassed them.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Taghiyah﴾: Allah sent upon them a cry which annihilated them.

The most correct of the two views regarding this is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: they were destroyed by the overwhelming cry.

The Lord says: ﴿Pharaoh came, and those before him, and the overturned cities, with sin﴾ (Egypt). The reciters differed over the reading of ﴿وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾. Most of the reciters of Medina, Kufa and Mecca, except al-Kisa'i, read ﴿وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the ba', meaning: "and those who came before Pharaoh from the nations that denied Allah's signs, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and the people of Lut, with sin." The reciters of Basra and al-Kisa'i read ﴿وَمَنْ قِبَلِهِ﴾ with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', meaning: "and those with him from the people of his land, Egypt, from the Copts."

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that both are well-known readings with sound meanings, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

That is, the villages that were overturned with their people, so that their uppermost part became their lowermost part. ﴿with sin﴾ means with sin (khati'ah). Their sin was having intercourse with males in their backsides.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said about the meaning of ﴿the overturned cities﴾.

The Lord says: ﴿Pharaoh came, and those before him, and the overturned cities, with sin﴾ (Egypt). The reciters differed over the reading of ﴿وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾. Most of the reciters of Medina, Kufa and Mecca, except al-Kisa'i, read ﴿وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the ba', meaning: "and those who came before Pharaoh from the nations that denied Allah's signs, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and the people of Lut, with sin." The reciters of Basra and al-Kisa'i read ﴿وَمَنْ قِبَلِهِ﴾ with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', meaning: "and those with him from the people of his land, Egypt, from the Copts."

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that both are well-known readings with sound meanings, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and the overturned cities with sin﴾

That is, the villages that were overturned with their people, so that their uppermost part became their lowermost part. ﴿with sin﴾ means with sin (khati'ah). Their sin was having intercourse with males in their backsides.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said about the meaning of ﴿the overturned cities﴾.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Pharaoh came, and those before him, and the overturned cities﴾: "the city of Lut." In some readings it is ﴿Pharaoh came, and those with him﴾.

And regarding His words: ﴿and the overturned one He hurled down﴾, he said: "He hurled them down from the sky. Allah revealed to Jibril (peace be upon him), and he uprooted it from the earth, its foundations and its town, then he dropped them to the sky, then he turned them upside down onto the earth, then he followed them with stones of baked clay." He recited the words of Allah: ﴿stones of baked clay, layered, marked﴾, and said: "The marked ones are those prepared for punishment."

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 69, verses 13–15:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast (13), and the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crushing (14), on that Day the Inevitable will occur (15)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Then when the Trumpet is blown﴾ by Israfil ﴿with a single blast﴾, which is the first blast. ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crushing﴾ means: they will be shaken with a single convulsion.

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crushing﴾, "They will become dust."

It was said: ﴿fa-dukkata﴾ (crushed, in dual form), although the mountains and the earth were mentioned before, and they are plural. It was not said "fa-dukkakna" (crushed, in plural form), because He treated the mountains as a single thing, just as the poet said:

"They are two lords who claim [to lead], but they lead us only if their goats have multiplied."

[[The author of Lisan (under y-s-r) attributes the verse to Abu Usayda al-Dubayri, and al-Ayni in his commentary on the shawahid of the Alfiyya attributes it likewise. Lisan cites before it another verse: "Indeed we have two shaykhs who benefit us not... rich in ways that their wealth does not profit us."

That is, there is no lordship in them except that their goats have multiplied, i.e., their flocks and their milk and offspring have increased; lordship requires generosity, giving, protection, defense, good management and forbearance, and they have none of these. The author cited the verse to show that the poet said "ghanamahuma" (their goats) in the dual form for the sheep, although "ghanam" is a collective noun and not a singular, but he treated it as a singular, just as the mountains were treated as singular in His saying (And the earth and the mountains were lifted up and crushed with a single crushing), being regarded as singular like "the earth," and therefore He said "fa-dukkata" and not "fa-dukkakna." End of quotation. The verse contains another point of evidence among the grammarians, in the section on the cancellation of the operation of ẓanna and the verbs of the heart when they are placed after their objects; had they preceded them, they would have governed them in the accusative.]]

﴿On that Day the Inevitable will occur﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: on that Day the Cry will occur, the Hour will be established, and the Resurrection will take place.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the heaven will be split and cleft, ﴿so it that Day will be frail﴾, meaning: split and cracked.

Those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to what we have said on this.

Whoever said that:

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, who said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God commands the lowest heaven with its inhabitants, and those of the angels who are in it descend and surround the earth and those upon it. When the people of the earth see it, they flee, but they do not reach any region of the earth without finding seven rows of angels, so they return to the place where they were. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 69, verse 22–24:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he will be in a pleasant life (21) In an elevated garden (22) Its fruits are near at hand (23) "Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you put forth in the days past." (24)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "So he who has been described" – and he is the one given his record in his right hand – "is in a pleasing life," or "a life in which there is contentment." The life is described as pleasing (radiya), though it is in fact pleasing (mardiyya), because that is praise for the life. The Arabs do this in praise and blame: they say "this is a sleeping night" (layl na'im), "a hidden secret" (sirr katim), and "a gushing water" (ma' dafiq), attributing the action to the thing, while in origin it is said of what is intended as praise or blame. Whoever says this is not permitted to say of the one who strikes "he is struck," nor of the one who is struck "he is striker," because there is no praise or blame in that.

* *

His saying: ﴿In an elevated garden﴾

He says: in a lofty, high orchard. The "in" in His saying ﴿in a garden﴾ is connected to "life."

* *

His saying: ﴿Its fruits are near at hand﴾

He says: what is plucked from the Garden of its fruits is near to the one who plucks it.

It has been mentioned that whoever wishes for its fruit may reach it however he wishes, standing or sitting; distance does not prevent him, and no thorn comes between him and it.

Those of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say concerning this verse, ﴿its fruits are near at hand﴾: "A man takes from its fruits while he is lying down."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿its fruits are near at hand﴾: "They are brought near, so that neither distance nor thorns keep their hands from them."

* *

His saying: ﴿"Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you put forth in the days past"﴾

Their Lord, great is His praise, says to them: "Eat, O company whom I have been pleased with and whom I have admitted into My garden, from its fruits, and the good of what is in it of foods; and drink from its drinks. Those of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said, God said: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you put forth in the days past﴾. - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿for what you put forth in the days past﴾: "The days of the world, by what they did in them."

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says, informing about this wretched one who was given his record in his left hand: indeed, in the world he did not urge people to feed the needy and the destitute.

* *

As related:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 69, verse 47–52:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So there is none of you who could withhold Us from him﴾ [47] ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for the God-fearing﴾ [48] ﴿And indeed We know that among you are deniers﴾ [49] ﴿And indeed it is a source of regret for the disbelievers﴾ [50] ﴿And indeed it is the certain truth﴾ [51] ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [52]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: There is none of you, O people, who could withhold Us from Muhammad, if he had fabricated some of the sayings against Us, so that We seized him by the right hand, then severed his aorta, [such that] there would be none who could keep Us back from punishing him and from doing to him what We do. It was said: "ḥājizīn" (withholders) is in the plural, while the verb "min aḥadin" (of anyone) is singular; the singular "aḥad" is used here to correspond to its meaning, since its sense is plural. The Arabs use "aḥad" for the singular, the dual and the plural, as in the saying ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾, and "bayn" (between) is only used with two or more.

* *

And His words: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for the God-fearing﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed this Qur'an is a reminder, meaning an admonition by which one remembers and is admonished, for the God-fearing, who are those who guard against the punishment of God by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobediences.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for the God-fearing﴾, he said: "The Qur'an."

* *

His words: ﴿And indeed We know that among you are deniers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And indeed We know that among you, O people, are those who deny this Qur'an. ﴿And indeed it is a source of regret for the disbelievers﴾. He, may His praise be exalted, says: Indeed denying it is a source of regret and remorse for the disbelievers in the Qur'an on the Day of Resurrection.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And indeed it is a source of regret for the disbelievers﴾: "That is the Day of Resurrection." ﴿And indeed it is the certain truth﴾ means: And indeed it is the absolute certain truth, about which there is no doubt that it is from God, and which Muhammad ﷺ did not fabricate. ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾, by mentioning your Lord and naming Him the Mighty, in whose greatness everything is small.
